title: GitHub fine-grained PAT spec
description: Declarative spec consumed by scripts/form.mjs to drive GitHub's fine-grained personal-access-token creation UI. There is NO API to create fine-grained PATs (web UI only), so this spec is the machine-readable SSoT the browser engine reads.

name.description: Token name. Must be unique on the account.

notes.description: Provenance, rationale and incident history for maintainers. NEVER typed into GitHub's UI — put long-form reasoning here, not in `description`, which is a real form field with a server-side length limit.

description.description: Free-text token description (optional). Typed verbatim into GitHub's description textarea. KEEP IT SHORT: the textarea advertises no maxlength (maxLength === -1), but the SERVER rejects an over-long one by re-rendering the blank form with NO error message anywhere on the page — the submit simply does nothing and no token is created. Measured 2026-09-04: 4272 chars failed silently and repeatedly, 191 chars succeeded on the next attempt with every other field byte-identical. Long-form rationale belongs in `notes`.

owner.description: Resource-owner login. Omit to use the authenticated user. Set to an org login for org-owned tokens.

expiration.description: Token lifetime: 7/30/60/90/366 (days), an ISO date 'YYYY-MM-DD' (custom), or 'none' (no expiration — triggers a confirm modal). 366 is only offered when the resource owner is an ORGANISATION that caps token lifetime, and in that case 'none' is NOT offered at all: an org limit removes the option rather than disabling it (measured 2026-09-04 against doorward-systems, which offers 7/30/60/90/366 + 'Custom between 1 and 366 days'). So a spec targeting an org may not be able to say 'none' however much you want it to.

repositoryAccess.description: Which repositories the token can touch. 'public' = read-only public repos (use for account-only tokens); 'all' = every repo the owner has; 'selected' = the explicit 'repos' list.

permissions.description: UI permission rows to set. Key = exact permission label as shown in GitHub's 'Add permissions' menu (e.g. 'Contents', 'Pull requests', 'Commit statuses', 'Gists'). Value: 'read' -> 'Read-only', 'write' -> 'Read and write'. 'Metadata' is auto-required read-only and must NOT be listed.
